newsitem.title: POLAND: Third Polish cellular phone firm to launch service.
newsitem.headline: Third Polish cellular phone firm to launch service.

text.p: The cellular telephone consortium of Polish and foreign firms Polkomtel SA will launch services in early October to become Poland's third mobile phone operator, Polkomtel spokesman said on Friday.

Leszek Kaminski told Reuters that Polkomtel, in which Danish telecom operator Tele Danmark and U.S. AirTouch Communications hold a 19.25 percent stake each, wanted to provide services in more than 20 of Poland's big cities and attract at least 30,000 customers by the end of the year.

Polkomtel plans to provide services to at least 100,000 customers by the end of 1997 across 80 percent of Poland. The company earlier said it would invest $1 billion by the year 2000 to attract one million customers.

Polkomtel, which groups Polish copper combine KGHM SA, Plock oil refinery and the National Power Grid (PSE), is one of the two firms which early this year won a licence to build a cellular network in a modern digital GSM system.
The other GSM company, PTC Era GSM SA, launched services earlier this month.

Era's shoreholders include US West of the United States and Deutsche Telekom's subsidiary DeTeMobil, with 22.5 percent stakes each and Polish conglomerate Elektrim SA, which controls 32.5 percent of shares.

The two cellular phone companies will compete with Centertel SA, a joint venture between Polish state-owned telecom firm TPSA, France Telecom and Ameritech Corp., which has been active in Poland since 1991 and has more than 100,000 customers.
Cetertel, which uses an older analogue cellular system, had not bid for a GSM licence because of internal conflict between TPSA and Centertel's foreign shareholders.
